Bleckede lies between the Geest and marshland and, with its 13 districts, stretches along the Elbe. The landscape of the Lower Saxon Elbe Valley Biosphere Reserve surrounds the town, offering nature experiences and opportunities to see rare animal species. River scenery, geological traces and historic buildings provide a range of themes to consider when planning your trip.

## The Elbe Valley and traces of the Ice Age

Bleckede Castle is home to the Biosphaerium Elbtalaue, an information and visitor centre for the Lower Saxon Elbe Valley Biosphere Reserve. Its modern exhibition spans more than 1,000 square metres and focuses on the birdlife and aquatic life of the Elbe Valley. This gives the landscape a tangible focal point: the region’s habitats take centre stage here.

Bleckede Castle’s tower also offers a view of the landscape: from its observation platform, you can enjoy a 360-degree panorama over Bleckede and the surrounding area. Another natural attraction awaits at the Erratic Boulder Ring in Breetze, a district of Bleckede. There, erratic boulders from the Ice Age illustrate how the Elbe glacial valley was formed.

A hiking route starts at the car park by the Biosphaerium Elbtalaue – Bleckede Castle. It follows the dike and a sandy path past old Elbe channels, oxbow bends and flood ponds, then crosses the lock on the “Alte Elbe” towards the Heisterbusch sheep farm. The landscape itself becomes the focus of the route: waterways and varied forms of riverbank shape its course.

## Castle, church and town tours

Bleckede Castle is a listed historic complex dating back several centuries. Its oldest part is the remains of a historic tower from the 13th century. St. James’ Church in Bleckede was rebuilt in 1766 in the late Baroque style. The castle and church thus represent two different chapters in the town’s architectural history.

Guided town tours are available for groups and can be arranged through the Tourist Information Centre. Lasting an hour or longer on request, they offer a visual, cultural and historical overview. If you are planning a group trip, the standard duration and option to extend it individually can help with your day’s itinerary.

## More to explore in the wider destination of Lüneburg

The wider destination of Lüneburg also offers its own cultural attractions. City and town hall tours in Lüneburg showcase its historic atmosphere, with gabled brick houses, old lanes and the waterside district. At Lüneburg Water Tower, an observation platform 56 metres above the ground offers views across the city and its surroundings. The tower hosts sophisticated concerts at 8 p.m. on the first Sunday of every month and at every full moon. Check the dates if you would like to include these concerts in your travel plans.

## Find accommodation to suit your travel interests

When choosing where to stay, it helps to first decide what you would like to focus on: Bleckede brings together the Elbe Valley, erratic boulders and local architectural history. Lüneburg adds city tours and the water tower to the wider destination. If your trip brings together different interests, these distinct themes can help you structure your plans. Choose your accommodation search based on the places and experiences you want to make the focus of your stay.
